region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Standing Stone Vineyards farms a slope in Hector, on the east side of Seneca Lake, where Gold Seal winemakers Charles Fournier and Guy Devaux planted Riesling and Chardonnay between 1972 and 1975, among the earliest vinifera vines in the Finger Lakes. Marti and Tom Macinski bought the farm in 1991 and built Standing Stone into one of the region’s pioneering estates. In 2017 Fred Merwarth and Oskar Bynke of Hermann J. Wiemer bought it, keeping Standing Stone as its own label.

Saperavi is the estate’s signature: an ancient Georgian grape whose flesh, not only its skin, is red, which is what “Teinturier” (French for dyer) on the label refers to. Standing Stone was one of the few wineries outside Georgia to grow it, releasing a first, 36-case Saperavi from the 2005 vintage. The 2023 comes from vines 10 to 25 years old, hand-picked and fermented with native yeast in stainless steel, about 15 percent as whole clusters. It then rested 10 months, roughly 70 percent in neutral Hungarian barrels of 225 and 500 liters and the rest in steel.
